bib.title: More Agents Is All You Need

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "More Agents Is All You Need" (Agent Forest), Junyou Li, Qin Zhang, Yangbin Yu, Qiang Fu, Deheng Ye (Tencent), Transactions on Machine Learning Research, Oct 2024 (arXiv 2402.05120v2).

COVERAGE: All 18 of 18 pages; 55,806 chars. I read the body (sampling, results, analysis, conclusion), the appendices (A settings, B.1 curves, B.2 ANOVA, B.3 token plot) and skimmed the references. Figure pixels were not viewed; only caption text. There is no separate limitations section. The target note (04-multi-agent-design-patterns.md) has no Li/Agent Forest citation. Line 348 has a "Multi-plan selection" row (majority vote) and line 408 covers RAP/rStar/PlanGEN. Relevant link: majority-vote baselines. Not "already covered" for this paper.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Sampling N times from the same LLM and majority-voting ("Agent Forest") raises accuracy as ensemble size grows, across 5 tasks and 3 models.
  number: 40-sample gains of +12 to +24 pts GSM8K, +6 to +10 MATH, +1 to +4 Chess, +5 to +11 MMLU, +4 to +9 HumanEval
  setup: Llama2-13B/70B-Chat, GPT-3.5-Turbo (0613); ensemble 40; mean of 10 runs
  quote: "the accuracy gains range from12% to 24% on the GSM8K and from6% to 10% on the MATH. In general reasoning tasks, the accuracy gains range from 1% to 4% on the Chess and from5% to 11% on the MMLU. In code generation task, the accuracy gains range from4% to 9% on HumanEval."
  where: p.6, Sec 5.1, Table 2
- A smaller model with voting beats a larger single model.
  number: Llama2-13B 59% vs Llama2-70B single 54% on GSM8K
  setup: ensemble 40 vs one query. The abstract and Fig 1 also say 70B voting ~ GPT-4 level (that comparison is in the figure and not backed by a quoted number).
  quote: "the enhanced Llama2-13B model achieves 59% accuracy on the GSM8K dataset, outperforming the Llama2-70B model, which scores54%."
  where: p.6; Table 2 and Fig 1
- Table 2 key rows (single to 40): GPT-3.5 GSM8K 0.73 to 0.85, MATH 0.29 to 0.39, MMLU 0.59 to 0.70; Llama2-70B GSM8K 0.54 to 0.74. GPT-4 single: GSM8K 0.88, MATH 0.40, MMLU 0.77, HumanEval 0.88.
  quote: "GPT-3.5-Turbo OpenAI (2022) 0.73 ± 2e-2 0.85 ± 3e-3 0.29 ± 2e-2 0.39 ± 2e-3 0.51 ± 3e-2 0.55 ± 2e-3 0.59 ± 3e-2 0.70 ± 2e-3 0.67 ± 2e-2 0.73 ± 1e-2"
  where: p.6, Table 2
- Voting alone matches or beats the heavier methods (CoT, Zero-shot CoT, SPP, Debate, Reflection) in most cases, and has the best average rank. Rank 2.5 overall vs Debate 4.4 (worst), Reflection 3.3, CoT 3.3, ZS-CoT 2.7, SPP 4.
  quote: "Ours 2.6 2.6 2.2 2.5" (Table 4; Debate row "3.8 4.4 5 4.4")
  quote2: "our method outperforms other methods in standalone cases, except on the Chess task using Llama2-13B and Llama2-70B."
  where: p.7-8, Sec 5.3, Table 4
  Caveat: the ranks are averaged over 5 tasks per model. Debate was capped at ensemble 10, versus 40 for the others.
- Voting stacks on top of other methods, but Debate is the exception on code.
  number: gains +10 to +21 GSM8K, +1 to +15 MATH, +1 to +13 Chess, +1 to +11 MMLU, +2 to +7 HumanEval. Debate+voting scored 0 on HumanEval for both Llama2 models (Table 3, "Debate ... 0 0").
  quote: "two notable exceptions are observed when integrated with the debate method with the Llama2-13B and Llama2-70B models, which result in failed cases. This failure in performance is attributed primarily to the noise generated by referencing the answers of other agents during the debate process."
  where: p.7, Sec 5.2, Table 3. The cause is the authors' attribution and was not tested.
- Gains grow with difficulty (relative gain η=(Pm−Ps)/Ps).
  number: GSM8K 69/37/16% and MATH 200/120/34% for Llama2-13B/Llama2-70B/GPT-3.5
  quote: "GSM8K (easy) 69 37 16 / MATH (hard) 200 120 34"
  where: p.9, Table 6. Caution: the large relative gains on MATH come from tiny base accuracies (0.03 to 0.09). The absolute gain is 6 pts.
- Three controlled-difficulty properties, using a synthetic task: find the interval of Σaᵢbᵢ, with I = integer range, S = steps, K = number of answer intervals (prior 1/K).
  (1) Gains rise then fall with inherent difficulty: "The most notable gains are seen atI = 100 and I = 200... atI = 400, gains taper off" (p.10).
  (2) Gains rise with steps: "4%-18% gains over {I = 10,K = 2} compared to 16%-48% over{I = 100,K = 4}" (p.10).
  (3) Accuracy rises with prior probability of the correct answer (p.11).
  setup: GPT-3.5-Turbo-1106, JSON mode, 40 samples vs 1, mean of 10 runs
- Step-wise Agent Forest (decompose, vote at each step, feed the result forward) beats plain voting.
  number: 15%-42% gains, S=8, K=4, I=100 to 400
  quote: "Step-wise Agent Forest yields greater improvements. e.g., we see15%-42% gains, which increase with inherent difficulty."
  where: p.11
- Hierarchical Agent Forest: cheap model solves a coarse version, a stronger model finishes.
  number: homogeneous GPT-3.5 21% to 31%. Heterogeneous (GPT-3.5 at K=8, then GPT-4 at K=32): 35% to 47% vs GPT-4 alone at K=32.
  quote: "improves performance from35% to 47%, suggesting the deployment of different LLMs at the corresponding level of problem-solving can improve the performance in a cost-effective manner."
  where: p.11, Fig 7 right. The cost saving is asserted, not measured.
- Robust to temperature T and nucleus p. Gains hold across settings (Fig 4; GPT-3.5, mean of 20 runs). One-way ANOVA across ensemble sizes (1,10,20,30,40) gives all p<0.05.
  quote: "all p-values are less than 0.05"
  where: p.8 (Sec 5.4), p.17-18 (Table 7; smallest effect HumanEval Llama2-13B 5.46e-8)
- Cost scales linearly with agents.
  number: single-agent GPT-3.5 tokens per sample: GSM8K 235, MATH 326, Chess 138, MMLU 247, HumanEval 495.
  quote: "the token usage increases proportionally with the number of agents or when combined with other methods."
  where: p.8, Table 5. At N=40 that is roughly 40x the single-call token count (my arithmetic, not stated).

Voting mechanism: closed-ended tasks use frequency; HumanEval uses cumulative sacreBLEU, and the sample with the highest summed similarity to the others wins.
  quote: "The sample that exhibits the highest cumulative similarity is then chosen as the final answer denoted as A = arg maxsi∈SV (si)."
  where: p.4, Algorithm 1, App A

LIMITS
- The authors concede cost: "such a challenge of escalating costs commonly exists in works requiring multiple LLM calls... We leave it as a future work to optimize." They note that sampling could be optimised because the input is identical. They cite Kapoor et al. 2024 on accuracy-only benchmarking.
- The single-run configuration of Debate is capped at ensemble 10 for overhead.
- Gains vanish at extreme difficulty (I=400) and are small for strong models and for Chess (+1 to +4 pts; 70B Chess only 0.12 to 0.13).
- Models are old (Llama2, GPT-3.5-0613, GPT-4-0613); no modern reasoning models. Section 6 uses different model versions (gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 with JSON mode) from Section 4.
- The "agents" are independent samples of one prompt, with no interaction or role differentiation. The title overstates the multi-agent angle.
- Voting needs an answer that can be extracted and compared. Open-ended tasks rely on BLEU similarity.
- GPT-4 was not given voting (a single result only).
- Mechanism claims (e.g. the cause of the Debate failure) are not tested.
- The synthetic difficulty task is a single arithmetic family.

BUILDS ON: Wang et al. 2023b (CoT-SC, self-consistency); Du et al. 2023 (LLM-Debate); Shinn et al. 2023 (Reflexion); Wei et al. 2022 (CoT); Kojima et al. 2022 (zero-shot CoT); Wang et al. 2023c (SPP); Fu et al. 2023 (Complexity-CoT); Breiman 2001 (Random Forests, name); Lu et al. 2024 (Blended); Chen et al. 2023b (FrugalGPT); Papineni et al. 2002 (BLEU); Wu et al. 2023 (AutoGen).

CODE
Algorithm 1 (p.4), pseudo-code verbatim in structure: sample S = {M(x)} for i=1..N; V(s_i) = sum over j≠i of sim(s_i, s_j); return A = argmax V(s_i).

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.2): accuracy vs ensemble size on GSM8K for Llama2-13B/70B/GPT-3.5, with single-model reference lines. It shows the small model catching the next size up in one view.
- Fig 2 (p.4): two-phase sampling + voting diagram.
- Fig 3 (p.6): accuracy curves for all 5 tasks x 3 models. Shows diminishing returns by size.
- Fig 5 and 6 (p.9-10): three difficulty dimensions and gain curves.
- Fig 7 (p.11): step-wise and hierarchical gains.
- Fig 14 (p.18): token usage vs accuracy, the cost trade-off.
I did not run the figure script and did not view the figures.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Extraction is clean apart from garbled plot axes and glued words. The first tool output was truncated by the harness; I re-read the remainder via a second extraction. The one-time 40000-char print omitted the appendix, which I then read. The word "orthogonal" in the abstract is the authors' wording for composability with other methods.
